chunks: Verily We gave Moses the Book; but they began to differ about it. If the Word of your Lord had not preceded it the matter would have been settled between them. They are still in doubt about it and uneasy.

key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: The Book (referring to the Torah or divine scripture)

ai.seo_question: Why did people differ about the Book of Moses and what is the role of divine decree in their judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Yunus underscores the inevitability of divine delay (Hikmah) in judgment to allow for human free will and the testing of faith amidst the divergent interpretations of the Torah. It highlights that the 'disagreement' (Ikhtilaf) among the Children of Israel serves as a precursor to the broader human condition of doubt, with the 'word' (Kalimah) referring to God's promise of patience until the appointed time. This context reinforces the Shia emphasis on the continuity of revelation and the role of divine wisdom in sustaining life despite textual and theological disputes.
